_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Nigeria covering Nok culture, Ife and Benin bronzes, Hausa-Fulani emirates, Oyo and Benin empires, Atlantic slave trade, British colonisation and indirect rule, Biafra civil war, oil economy, military dictatorships, Fourth Republic, and Boko Haram insurgency.

ethnic_groups.name: Hausa
ethnic_groups.notes: Largest group; northern Nigeria; Hausa city-states heritage; predominantly Muslim; intermarried with Fulani post-jihad; Hausa language widest-spoken in West Africa

ethnic_groups.name: Yoruba
ethnic_groups.notes: Southwestern Nigeria; Oyo Empire and Ife kingdom heritage; complex Orisha religious tradition; Lagos/Ibadan; Nollywood

ethnic_groups.name: Igbo (Ibo)
ethnic_groups.notes: Southeastern Nigeria; republican/decentralised tradition; Biafra War 1967–1970; commercial dynamism; Christianity dominant

ethnic_groups.name: Fulani (Fulbe/Peul)
ethnic_groups.notes: Pastoralists and settled; Sokoto Caliphate heritage (Usman dan Fodio); northern Nigeria; Muslim; Fulani-herder conflicts

ethnic_groups.name: Ijaw
ethnic_groups.notes: Niger Delta; Nigeria's fourth-largest; oil-producing region; MEND militants; Isaac Adaka Boro's republic; Bayelsa

ethnic_groups.name: Kanuri
ethnic_groups.notes: Northeastern Nigeria; Borno State; Kanem-Bornu Empire (1000+ years); Boko Haram heartland

ethnic_groups.name: Ibibio
ethnic_groups.notes: Akwa Ibom State; southeastern coast; related to Annang and Efik

ethnic_groups.name: Tiv
ethnic_groups.notes: Benue State; Middle Belt; segmentary society; historically resisted centralised authority

ethnic_groups.name: Nupe
ethnic_groups.notes: Niger and Kwara States; Nupe Kingdom; Middle Belt

ethnic_groups.name: Edo/Bini
ethnic_groups.notes: Benin City; Benin Empire and Benin Bronzes; Oba of Benin; Edo State

ethnic_groups.name: Igala
ethnic_groups.notes: Kogi State; ancient Igala kingdom; confluence of Niger and Benue

ethnic_groups.name: Efik
ethnic_groups.notes: Cross River State; Calabar; historical trade and European contact; Old Calabar slave trade

ethnic_groups.name: Other (250+ ethnic groups)
ethnic_groups.notes: Nigeria has over 250 ethnic groups; Jukun, Idoma, Berom, Ebira, Gwari, Ogoni (Ken Saro-Wiwa), etc.; extreme diversity

country_profile.notes_unique: Most populous country in Africa; largest economy in Africa by GDP

natural_resources.notes: Africa's largest oil producer (~1.4 mbpd); NNPC (national oil company); Niger Delta (Bonny Light crude); massive natural gas reserves (~200 tcf, largely flared); oil theft ($3-5B/year); agriculture employs 35%+ of workforce; Nigerian cocoa fourth globally; palm oil; solid minerals sector underdeveloped.

military.notes: Africa's largest military by personnel; fighting Boko Haram/ISWAP insurgency in northeast (14+ years); banditry in northwest; separatist agitation (IPOB/Biafra); ECOMOG intervention force in Liberia/Sierra Leone (1990s); equipment modernisation ongoing.

infrastructure.notes: MTN, Airtel, Glo, 9mobile; Lagos congestion crisis; Dangote group (largest conglomerate); 5G launched 2022 by MTN/Mafab.

debt_aid.notes: Africa's largest economy by GDP; Sovereign Wealth Authority (NSIA); fuel subsidy removal 2023 (~$10B/year savings); naira devaluation 2023-24; debt servicing exceeds revenue; Dangote Refinery ($19B, Africa's largest) operational 2024.

education.notes: ~20 million out-of-school children (world's highest); massive north-south education gap; ASUU strikes paralyse public universities; private universities growing; 13-million child 'almajiri' system in north; JAMB admission bottleneck.

diaspora_migration.diaspora_population: 15 million+ (USA, UK, Canada, South Africa, Ghana, Cameroon, globally)
diaspora_migration.notes: Largest African diaspora globally; 'Japa' phenomenon (youth emigration surge post-2020); remittances ~4% GDP; Nigerian professionals prominent in US/UK health, tech sectors; Boko Haram displaced 2.2 million internally; Cameroonian refugees hosted.
diaspora_migration.immigration_policy: ECOWAS free movement; 'japa' emigration wave (UK, Canada, USA)

digital_economy.notes: Africa's largest tech ecosystem; multiple unicorns (Flutterwave, OPay, Interswitch); Paystack acquired by Stripe; MTN, Airtel, Glo, 9mobile operators; NIN digital identity rollout; fintech leads innovation; Lagos startup ecosystem attracts global VC.

country_profile.national_motto: Unity and Faith, Peace and Progress
country_profile.national_anthem: Nigeria, We Hail Thee / Arise, O Compatriots (adopted 2024)

geography.terrain: Coastal mangrove swamps; Niger Delta; tropical rainforest (south); Guinea savanna (central); Sudan savanna (north); Jos Plateau; Lake Chad Basin
geography.notes: Africa's most populous country (~230M); 'Giant of Africa'; Niger Delta oil region; 36 states + FCT; 250+ ethnic groups; 500+ languages.

economy_extended.notes: Africa's largest economy; oil dependent (#1 in Africa, OPEC member); Dangote refinery (650kbpd, Africa's largest); tech hub (Lagos: 'Africa's Silicon Valley'); naira devaluation 2023; fuel subsidy removal; Nollywood industry.

health.notes: Worst maternal mortality globally (917/100k); polio eradicated (2020, WHO certified); brain drain (japa phenomenon); NHIS expansion; malaria #1 global burden (25% of world's cases).

food_agriculture.notes: World's #1 cassava and yam producer; cocoa exports; herder-farmer conflicts (Fulani); rice import-substitution efforts; Agricultural Transformation Agenda.

energy.notes: OPEC member; Dangote refinery (650kbpd, commissioned 2023-24); oil theft/pipeline vandalism; gas flaring; chronic power outages ('generator republic'); planned Mambilla hydropower (3050MW).

transport.national_airline: Nigeria Air (planned, not launched) / Air Peace (largest private)
transport.notes: Lagos-Ibadan rail (standard gauge, Chinese-built); Abuja Metro (light rail); Lagos gridlock notorious; Lekki Deep Sea Port (2023).

tourism.notes: Business tourism dominates; cultural tourism potential; security (Boko Haram, banditry) deters leisure visitors; diaspora return tourism.

human_rights_gender.lgbtq_legal_status: Illegal (14 years; death penalty in Sharia states)
human_rights_gender.notes: 12 northern states apply Sharia; VAPP Act (Violence Against Persons); EndSARS protests (2020, Lekki toll gate); press freedom concerns; IPOB/Biafra separatist movement.

border_disputes: Bakassi Peninsula (settled by ICJ 2002 in favor of Cameroon)
security_stability.notes: Multi-front security challenges; Boko Haram (since 2009, 40,000+ killed, millions displaced); NW banditry escalating; IPOB/ESN in SE; 3M+ IDPs.

music_art_traditions: Afrobeats (Burna Boy, Wizkid, Davido, Tiwa Savage)
Nok terracotta (oldest in sub-Saharan Africa, 500 BC)
cultural_heritage.film_industry: Nollywood—2nd largest globally by output (2500+ films/year); $7B+ industry; global influence
cultural_heritage.media_landscape: NTA (state); Channels TV, AIT, TVC (private); Punch, Guardian, Vanguard (newspapers); largest media market in Africa; Afrobeats global cultural export
cultural_heritage.notes: Africa's cultural powerhouse; Afrobeats global phenomenon; Nollywood; 250+ ethnic groups; 3 dominant: Yoruba, Igbo, Hausa-Fulani; Nok civilization; Benin Kingdom.

legal_system.legal_tradition: English common law; Sharia law (12 northern states); customary law
legal_system.sharia_applicability: Full Sharia (criminal, civil) in 12 northern states since 2000
legal_system.customary_law_role: Customary courts in southern states; Area Courts in north
legal_system.notes: Federal system (36 states + FCT); triple legal system (common law, Sharia, customary); Supreme Court; EFCC anti-corruption commission.

comparative_rankings._note: Country position relative to continent and global.
comparative_rankings.notes: Africa's largest economy and most populous nation.

current_leader.name: Bola Ahmed Tinubu
current_leader.title: President
current_leader.notes: APC; former Lagos governor; 'Asiwaju' (leader); fuel subsidy removal; naira reforms; contested election vs Obi and Atiku

former_leaders.name: Nnamdi Azikiwe
former_leaders.notes: First Republic president (ceremonial); Igbo leader; 'Zik of Africa'; previously Governor-General 1960–1963

former_leaders.name: Yakubu Gowon
former_leaders.notes: Military head of state; Biafra War; 'No victor, no vanquished'; 12-state structure; oil boom

former_leaders.name: Murtala Muhammed
former_leaders.notes: Reformist military ruler; assassinated in Dimka coup attempt; Abuja decision

former_leaders.name: Olusegun Obasanjo
former_leaders.notes: Military ruler then elected president; handed power to Shagari 1979; returned 1999 as first Fourth Republic president; PDP

former_leaders.name: Shehu Shagari
former_leaders.notes: Second Republic; NPN; overthrown by Buhari

former_leaders.name: Muhammadu Buhari
former_leaders.notes: Military ruler 1983–85; returned as elected president 2015 (APC); anti-corruption; economic challenges

former_leaders.name: Ibrahim Babangida
former_leaders.notes: 'IBB'; Structural Adjustment; annulled June 12, 1993 election (MKO Abiola); 'stepped aside'

former_leaders.name: Sani Abacha
former_leaders.notes: Most repressive military dictator; Ken Saro-Wiwa execution; international isolation; died in office

former_leaders.name: Umaru Yar'Adua
former_leaders.notes: PDP; first Nigerian leader to acknowledge election flaws; died in office

former_leaders.name: Goodluck Jonathan
former_leaders.notes: First Niger Delta president; PDP; Chibok girls kidnapping; lost to Buhari 2015; first sitting president to concede peacefully

910.name: Ancient Civilisations of Nigeria
910.description: Nok culture terracottas; early ironworking; foundational cultures of the Nigerian region.

sub_clusters.name: Nok Culture
sub_clusters.description: Nok terracotta sculptures in central Nigeria; earliest known large-scale iron smelting in West Africa; distinctive artistic tradition.

sub_clusters.name: Early Iron Age Communities
sub_clusters.description: Ironworking spreads across Nigeria; foundation for later Yoruba, Igbo, and other civilisations.

910.name: Kingdom of Ife
910.description: Ife as spiritual and artistic centre of Yorubaland; naturalistic bronze and terracotta heads.

sub_clusters.name: Ife Bronze and Terracotta Art
sub_clusters.description: Naturalistic bronze heads produced using lost-wax casting; Ooni of Ife as spiritual progenitor of Yoruba kingdoms.

sub_clusters.name: Igbo-Ukwu Bronze Culture
sub_clusters.description: Sophisticated bronze casting at Igbo-Ukwu; evidence of long-distance trade; early Igbo political complexity.

920.name: Medieval States and Empires
920.description: Hausa city-states, Kanem-Bornu in the northeast, Benin Kingdom, and Oyo Empire emerge as major powers.

sub_clusters.name: Hausa City-States (Hausa Bakwai)
sub_clusters.description: Kano, Katsina, Zaria, and other walled city-states; trans-Saharan trade; leather, textile, and dye industries.

sub_clusters.name: Kanem-Bornu Empire in Northeast Nigeria
sub_clusters.description: Mai (king) dynasty; Birni Gazargamo capital; Islam adopted early; controls Lake Chad basin trade routes.

sub_clusters.name: Kingdom of Benin
sub_clusters.description: Edo people's powerful kingdom; Oba dynasty; renowned Benin Bronzes; Portuguese contact from 1485.

sub_clusters.name: Oyo Empire
sub_clusters.description: Yoruba military empire; cavalry power; Alaafin constitutional system; dominates southwestern Nigeria.

930.name: Atlantic Slave Trade and Nigeria
930.description: Nigeria as major source of enslaved Africans; Bight of Benin and Bight of Biafra; internal wars fuelled by trade.

sub_clusters.name: Bight of Benin Slave Coast
sub_clusters.description: Millions exported through Lagos, Badagry, and coastal ports; Oyo and Dahomey wars produce captives.

sub_clusters.name: Bight of Biafra and Igbo Hinterland
sub_clusters.description: Old Calabar, Bonny, and Elem Kalabari as slave ports; Aro Confederacy controls hinterland trade networks.

sub_clusters.name: Sokoto Caliphate (Fulani Jihad)
sub_clusters.description: Usman dan Fodio's jihad overthrows Hausa kings; Sokoto Caliphate becomes Africa's largest 19th-century state.

940.name: British Colonisation and Amalgamation
940.description: British annexation of Lagos; Royal Niger Company; Lugard's indirect rule; amalgamation 1914; colonial economy.

sub_clusters.name: Annexation of Lagos and Oil Rivers
sub_clusters.description: British bombard Lagos 1851; Crown Colony 1861; Oil Rivers Protectorate; palm oil trade replaces slave trade.

sub_clusters.name: Royal Niger Company and Conquest
sub_clusters.description: George Goldie's chartered company; conquest of Ilorin, Nupe, and Sokoto Caliphate; British control consolidated.

sub_clusters.name: Lugard's Amalgamation and Indirect Rule
sub_clusters.description: Frederick Lugard amalgamates Northern and Southern Nigeria 1914; indirect rule through traditional chiefs; Aba Women's War 1929.

sub_clusters.name: Nigerian Nationalism and Constitutional Advance
sub_clusters.description: Nnamdi Azikiwe, Obafemi Awolowo, Ahmadu Bello lead regional parties; Richards and Macpherson constitutions; path to independence.

950.name: Independence and First Republic
950.description: Independence 1960; federal structure; regional tensions; census crises; 1966 coups.

sub_clusters.name: Independence of Nigeria
sub_clusters.description: Nigeria independent 1 October 1960; Abubakar Tafawa Balewa PM; republic 1963; Azikiwe president.

sub_clusters.name: First Republic Political Crises
sub_clusters.description: Western Region crisis; rigged 1964 elections; Tiv riots; January and July 1966 coups.

950.name: Nigerian Civil War (Biafra)
950.description: Eastern Region secedes as Republic of Biafra; devastating civil war; famine; 1–3 million dead.

sub_clusters.name: Biafra Secession and War
sub_clusters.description: Ojukwu declares Biafra May 1967; federal blockade; Biafran famine shocks the world; surrender January 1970.

950.name: Military Rule and Oil Boom
950.description: Post-war military regimes; oil boom and bust; Murtala/Obasanjo, Buhari, Babangida, Abacha dictatorships.

sub_clusters.name: Oil Boom and Dutch Disease
sub_clusters.description: OPEC-era oil revenues transform economy; agriculture neglected; corruption and mega-projects; oil bust 1980s.

sub_clusters.name: Babangida and Abacha Military Dictatorships
sub_clusters.description: Babangida annuls June 12 1993 election; Abacha seizes power; executes Ken Saro-Wiwa 1995; international pariah.

960.name: Fourth Republic and Contemporary Nigeria
960.description: Democratic Fourth Republic; Obasanjo-Yar'Adua-Jonathan-Buhari-Tinubu presidencies; Boko Haram; Niger Delta militancy; economic diversification.

sub_clusters.name: Fourth Republic Democratic Transition
sub_clusters.description: Olusegun Obasanjo elected 1999; anti-corruption efforts (EFCC); debt relief; Sharia law expansion in north.

sub_clusters.name: Boko Haram Insurgency
sub_clusters.description: Mohammed Yusuf's Boko Haram escalates after 2009 crackdown; Chibok kidnapping 2014; northeast devastation; ISWAP faction.

sub_clusters.name: Niger Delta Militancy and Oil Pollution
sub_clusters.description: MEND attacks on oil infrastructure; amnesty programme 2009; Ogoniland environmental devastation; resource justice.

sub_clusters.name: Tinubu Presidency and Reforms
sub_clusters.description: Bola Tinubu elected 2023; fuel subsidy removal; naira devaluation; economic pain and reform ambitions.
